One perceptor research run (course-production/research/2026-09-24-melanotan-afamelanotide-melanocortin-skin/, 21 candidates) contributed Böhm 2025. Nothing is included on the strength of a guide reference alone.
grader: Graded 2026-09-24 by the agent under Omar Saleem's delegation ("you should be able to do that from the guide"); rule set below; final review Dr. Hannah-Shmouni
gradingRule: Grade = certainty the source gives for the specific clinical statement the lesson makes, on the guides' A–D scale. A: consistent large RCTs or approval-grade evidence. B: at least one well-designed, adequately powered RCT or an independent, quality-stratified meta-analysis (either direction). C: small or sponsor-funded RCTs without independent replication, or pooled trials dominated by them. D: animal, in-vitro, mechanistic, case series, manufacturer dossiers. 'context' = history, reviews used for framing, trial registrations without results, analytical or regulatory records (regulatory records are primary for status statements, not graded for efficacy). Where the two guides disagree, the lesson states both and the claim takes the grade the primary evidence supports. Observational studies (added 2026-09-24, GRADE starting point, for the final reviewer to confirm): adequately sized cohort, case-control or cross-sectional studies grade C for the association they measured; small or single-centre ones grade D; any causal claim drawn from observational data grades D. Meta-analyses of observational studies grade at most B, and only for association. Guidelines and consensus statements are 'context', cited for what they recommend, not graded as evidence.

claims.text: Human scalp hair follicles kept alive ex vivo respond to CRH by making POMC products (ACTH, α-MSH) and secreting cortisol, with HPA-like negative feedback, and ex vivo they also operate a GH/IGF-1-like somatotropic loop — a mechanism from organ-culture studies.
claims.reviewNote: mechanism register only; organ culture from one group

claims.text: Androgenetic alopecia is mediated by dihydrotestosterone: locally, 5α-reductase converts testosterone to DHT, which miniaturises genetically susceptible scalp follicles.
claims.reviewNote: consensus background; taught as mechanism

claims.text: Growing (anagen) hair follicles are immune-privileged; collapse of that privilege, with NKG2D+ CD8 T-cell and NK-cell infiltration of the bulb, is an essential prerequisite for alopecia areata.
claims.reviewNote: mechanism review

claims.text: In two phase 3 RCTs (BRAVE-AA1 and -AA2; 1,200 adults with severe alopecia areata; funded by Eli Lilly), baricitinib was superior to placebo: 38.8% and 35.9% on the higher dose reached SALT ≤20 at week 36, versus 6.2% and 3.3% on placebo. In the US, FDA approved baricitinib for adults with severe alopecia areata on 13 June 2022.
claims.reviewNote: A&RE grades A; numbers from the NEJM abstract; approval letter read
claims.gradeDecision: A — two large consistent RCTs + approval

claims.text: The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide's first-pass hair-loss workup: patterned thinning → androgenetic alopecia (topical minoxidil; finasteride in men; treat coexisting iron or thyroid problems); diffuse shedding after a trigger → telogen effluvium (remove the trigger, reassure, recheck ferritin and TSH); patchy smooth loss (± nail pitting) → alopecia areata (dermatology referral; screen thyroid and autoimmune disease); signs of androgen excess → hyperandrogenism work-up; always ferritin and TSH, androgens if virilising, biopsy a scarring pattern; refer severe or rapidly progressive alopecia areata promptly.
claims.reviewNote: the guide's own recommendation (algorithm p.93, a figure transcribed from the rendered page; referral list ch.5) — guide sufficient
claims.gradeDecision: guide recommendation — reported as the guide's algorithm

claims.text: A systematic review and meta-analysis of good- or fair-quality RCTs found topical minoxidil (in men and in women) and oral finasteride (in men) superior to placebo for androgenetic alopecia.
claims.reviewNote: evidence register; heterogeneity noted

claims.text: In the US (Drugs@FDA, checked 24 September 2026), topical minoxidil has been approved since 1988 and is marketed over the counter; finasteride for hair loss (Propecia) has been a prescription drug since 1997.
claims.reviewNote: regulatory register, US only; no strengths or doses taught

claims.text: Skin cells produce POMC and its products ACTH, α-MSH and β-endorphin and carry their receptors. Of the five melanocortin receptors, MC1R mediates pigmentation of skin and hair, MC2R adrenal steroidogenesis, MC3R and MC4R central control of food intake, and MC5R sebogenesis; true receptor distribution is probably wider than this map.
claims.reviewNote: mechanism register; the open-question caveat is Laiho's

claims.text: Afamelanotide is an MC1R agonist. In two sponsor-funded phase 3 RCTs in erythropoietic protoporphyria it increased pain-free time in direct sunlight (US trial, n=94: median 69.4 vs 40.8 hours over six months; EU trial, n=74: 6.0 vs 0.8 hours over nine months, with fewer phototoxic reactions). Both guides grade it A for EPP. Use outside EPP remains investigational (for example a phase 3 vitiligo trial started in 2023 with no results posted).
claims.reviewNote: evidence register (EPP only) plus a separate open-question sentence

claims.text: Afamelanotide (Scenesse) was authorised in the EU on 22 December 2014, under exceptional circumstances, for prevention of phototoxicity in adults with EPP, and approved in the US in 2019 to increase pain-free light exposure in adults with a history of phototoxic reactions from EPP. The current US label (revised August 2024) warns it may darken pre-existing naevi and freckles and recommends a full-body skin examination twice yearly.
claims.reviewNote: regulatory register, EU and US dated; UK status not asserted

claims.text: Melanotan II is a non-selective melanocortin agonist (MC1R, MC3R, MC4R, MC5R) that crosses into the brain. Its only controlled human data are a 1996 single-blind pilot in three men (tanning in two; nausea, yawning, spontaneous erections, somnolence) and a 1998 crossover in ten men with psychogenic erectile dysfunction; no trial has tested cosmetic tanning. The Peptide Pocket Guide grades it C and the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide D ('harms > benefit'); the course grades cosmetic use D.
claims.reviewNote: guides disagree — the lesson states both and takes the grade the primary evidence supports (author finding 1)
claims.gradeDecision: D for tanning — 3-volunteer pilot; C only for the erectogenic effect

claims.text: Reported harms of Melanotan II come from case reports and reviews: darkening and growth of existing naevi, eruptive and atypical (dysplastic) naevi, melanonychia; at least five melanomas reported during or after use, each in a person with other risk factors, so causation is unproven; ischaemic priapism needing surgery; sympathomimetic toxicity with rhabdomyolysis and renal dysfunction; FDA also lists posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome among published serious events.
claims.reviewNote: case-report evidence; causation for melanoma stated as unproven, as A&RE and Habbema do

claims.text: Melanotan II sold online is of uncertain content: vials from three online shops held 43–88% of the labelled amount, with up to 5.9% unknown impurities, and TGA testing of five identically labelled seized nasal sprays found content varying more than twofold between bottles.
claims.reviewNote: analytical records

claims.text: Melanotan II is approved for no therapeutic indication. US: FDA's compounding safety page (current as of 22 April 2026) lists it among nominations withdrawn from Category 2, citing impurity and immunogenicity risks and published reports of melanoma, PRES, sympathomimetic toxidrome and priapism. UK: MHRA (FOI 24/274, 17 April 2024) classes injectable products as medicines, says unauthorised medicines may not be sold, supplied or advertised, and advises users to stop immediately. Australia: TGA (17 August 2026) — prescription-only medicine, not approved as a tanning agent, no product on the ARTG.
claims.reviewNote: regulatory register, three jurisdictions dated; EU not asserted; TGA read from a 26 Aug 2026 archive capture

claims.text: The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide treats a personal or family history of melanoma as an absolute contraindication to Melanotan II. A case report describes crops of new atypical naevi and growth of existing naevi in a man with prior melanoma who self-injected an α-MSH analogue, with lightening after he stopped; MC1R activation does not prevent melanoma, and regular skin examination remains critical in high-risk people.
claims.reviewNote: the guide's recommendation, supported by case-level evidence

claims.text: Skin monitoring matters with melanocortin agonists: during Melanotan II use, sequential videodermoscopy documented naevus changes that made naevus and melanoma hard to tell apart, and even the approved MC1R agonist's US label recommends a full-body skin examination twice yearly.
claims.reviewNote: supports the case's 'examine, dermoscopy, refer' move; no surveillance interval is taught for Melanotan II

claims.text: PTD-DBM fuses a cell-penetrating TAT fragment to a sequence that competes CXXC5 off Dishevelled, activating Wnt/β-catenin; in mice it accelerated hair regrowth and wound-induced follicle neogenesis, and CXXC5 is raised in human balding scalp. This single 2017 study from the developer's group is its whole evidence: no human trial is published (PubMed) or registered (ClinicalTrials.gov) as of 24 September 2026. The Peptide Pocket Guide grades it D.
claims.reviewNote: absence of human trials checked live 2026-09-24

claims.text: A 2025 review's abstract speaks of 'clinical efficacy' for peptides such as PTD-DBM, but its own table describes PTD-DBM as unapproved and shown in mouse models, and flags an untested theoretical risk: off-target Wnt activation is associated with colorectal and hepatocellular carcinomas.
claims.reviewNote: appraisal point plus open question; no human safety data exist either way

claims.text: Thymulin is a nine-residue thymic peptide that is biologically active only when zinc-bound. No indexed human study of zinc thymulin for hair was found (the Peptide Pocket Guide's cited case series could not be located); its proposed hair mechanism is undefined, and whether any effect comes from the peptide or the zinc is unresolved. The Peptide Pocket Guide grades it D.
claims.reviewNote: absence statement after PubMed search 2026-09-24 (author finding 5)

claims.text: In the US, on FDA's 503A category lists of 14 May 2026, thymulin acetate sits in Category 3 (nominated without adequate support, not eligible for the Category 1 policy) and PTD-DBM appears in no category; neither is on the 503A bulks list (21 CFR 216.23).
claims.reviewNote: regulatory register, US only, dated

authorFindings: Grade disagreement between the guides — Melanotan II is GRADE C in the Pocket Guide and GRADE D ('harms > benefit') in A&RE ch.15. The only controlled human data are Dorr 1996 (single-blind, alternating-day pilot in three men, not randomized) and Wessells 1998 (ten-man erectile-dysfunction crossover); no trial has tested tanning. The course states both grades and teaches D for cosmetic use; the Pocket Guide may wish to align.

PPG-Aug Melanotan II references — 'Multiple case reports … (see TGA/MHRA warnings) [not indexed]': the case reports are indexed. The course adds Habbema 2017 (A&RE ch.15 ref 8), Cardones 2009, Paurobally 2013, Hjuler 2014, Mang 2012, Mallory 2021 and Nelson 2012, and the live regulator records: FDA's compounding safety page (current as of 22 Apr 2026), MHRA FOI 24/274 (17 Apr 2024) and TGA's safety advisory (17 Aug 2026). The Dorr 1996 reference carries no PMID in the guide (PMID 8637402).

A&RE ch.15 — Melanotan II 'unapproved by the FDA and by regulators in the UK, EU, and Australia': UK and Australia verified (MHRA 2024; TGA 2026); EU status was not checked against an EMA record, so the course names the US, UK and Australia only. A&RE ch.6 grades Melanotan II D beside 'no quality control'; the TGA 2026 testing (content varying more than twofold across identically labelled bottles) and Breindahl 2015 (43–88% of the labelled amount) are citable support.

PPG-Aug PTD-DBM entry — (a) 'Effective only combined with a Wnt-pathway modulator (typically valproic acid)': Lee 2017's abstract reports that the competitor peptide alone accelerated hair regrowth in mice (valproic acid was studied separately, including in CXXC5-knockout mice); the course teaches no combination claim. (b) The 'hair-shedding phase during early use' adverse reaction has no human source. (c) 'Used in compounding pharmacies': PTD-DBM appears in none of FDA's 503A categories (14 May 2026) and is not on the bulks list (21 CFR 216.23); a dated US status line would help. (d) The corresponding author is affiliated with CK Biotechnology Inc.

PPG-Aug Zinc Thymulin entry — 'Caroleo MC et al. (zinc thymulin hair-loss case series, small) [not indexed]' could not be located on PubMed or by author search. FDA's 14 May 2026 list places thymulin acetate in 503A Category 3 (nominated without adequate support), which the entry's 'compounded for cosmetic hair use' does not mention.

PPG-Aug Afamelanotide entry — 'Three pivotal Phase 3 trials … across 244 EPP adults' and '10-year post-authorization safety data show no new signals' were not verified; the course cites the two published NEJM trials (Langendonk 2015, n=74 and n=94). The current US label (revised Aug 2024) recommends a full-body skin examination twice yearly — worth quoting in the entry's safety line. A&RE ch.6 wording ('approved to reduce phototoxicity in EPP') matches the EMA indication; the US indication is 'to increase pain free light exposure in adult patients with a history of phototoxic reactions from EPP'.

A&RE hair-loss workup algorithm (p.93) is a figure with no extractable text; the course transcribed it from the rendered page (patterned thinning → AGA; diffuse shed after trigger → telogen effluvium; patchy smooth loss → alopecia areata; androgen excess → hyperandrogenism work-up; always ferritin and TSH, androgens if virilising, scarring → biopsy). Please confirm the transcription.

Not in either guide, worth adding — Adil & Godwin 2017 (RCT meta-analysis for minoxidil and finasteride), Böhm 2025 (MC1R activation review: approved agonists, at least five melanomas with Melanotan II all with other risk factors, skin examination in high-risk people), Laiho & Murray 2022 (receptor map, open access), Breindahl 2015 and Mang 2012 (dermoscopic changes during Melanotan II use).

Trial-registry caution — ClinicalTrials.gov records from the sponsor 'Hudson Biotech' include NCT07437560 (Melanotan II with NB-UVB for vitiligo, 'recruiting' since Feb 2026), whose summary begins 'This example interventional study record describes…', and NCT07481734, titled '(Mock Study)'. The same sponsor holds NCT07437586 (GHK-Cu wound gel) and NCT07437547 (BPC-157 hamstring), which module 04 cites as recruiting trials; they should be re-verified before either guide cites them as real trials. The course does not cite NCT07437560.
